title: Pioneer Kits — partnership scout notes
content:
Snapshot: quick scout of Pioneer Kits (PK). Maker- and STEM-focused K‑12 company: physical STEM kits + teacher portal + student-facing AR app. Small business (~60 employees), HQ in Portland. Selling direct to districts and via a handful of reseller partners. Recent press: grant from state STEM fund (Sep 2024) — good timing for budgeted pilot asks for 2025. Why worth pursuing: demo-friendly product, clear teacher workflows, potential to surface LLM-driven lesson plan generation and assessment summarization. Fits Redwood play: embedded inference for teacher-facing tooling with predictable latency and private deployment needs for districts.

Key people (research):
- CEO: Marcus Valdez — investor background, public messaging about scaling district deals.
- Head of Product: Anika Bose — owns teacher portal roadmap, likely decision influencer for integrations.
- Director of Partnerships: Omar Ebrahimi — manages resellers and pilot programs; primary sales contact possibility.
- Curriculum Lead: Dana Park — will evaluate pedagogical quality and safety.

Notes from website / outreach signals:
- Pricing model: per-kit + annual portal subscription. District contracts typical 1–3 years.
- Tech stack clues: React front-end, mentions of edge/mobile AR; likely uses AWS. No obvious in-house ML team (outsources CV/AR).
- Recent job posts: Senior Product Manager (teacher tools) — growth hire.

Hypotheses for value prop (test quickly):
1) Teacher time-savings: auto-generate differentiated lesson plans from kit content + student data.
2) Assessment summarization: use embeddings+routing to produce concise KPI reports per class (privacy + hosting matters).
3) Offline/edge-friendly inference: quantized small model + private deployment in district VPC for PII-sensitive student data.

Outbound sequence (short):
- Step 0: Intro research email to Omar (Director of Partnerships). Attach 1‑pager: "Pilot: AI lesson drafts + assessment summary (4‑week)". Call out: low-effort integration via Redwood SDK, cost estimate for 1 district pilot.
- Day 3: Follow-up w/ short demo gif + quick ROI note (teacher hours saved estimate).
- Day 10: LinkedIn message to Anika + share case study of similar company (anonymized).
- If positive: propose 20‑30m sync + technical checklist for pilot (data flows, hosting, auth).

Cold email draft (subject + short body):
Subject: Pilot idea — auto lesson drafts for Pioneer Kits teachers
Hi Omar — noticed Pioneer Kits just closed the state STEM grant (congrats). Quick thought: we can stand up a 4‑week pilot that auto-generates teacher lesson drafts + end‑of‑week class summaries using your kit content and a small private LLM. No student data leaves district VPC; integration is a single webhook and optional SDK. Can I share a 1‑page pilot plan and a rough cost estimate?
— Samira (Redwood Inference)

Anticipated objections & suggested rebuttals (practice snippets):
- Objection: "We don't want student data out of our network."
  Rebuttal: "We support private deployments (VPC or on‑prem). Pilot can run entirely inside the district's cloud project; we provide audit logs and KMS/HSM hooks — minimal changes to current infra."
- Objection: "We can't add more vendor integrations for 2025 budget."
  Rebuttal: "Pilot scoped to 4 weeks, capped cost, and designed to show teacher time savings (estimate 1 hour/week per teacher). If it moves adoption, we can fold into next year's subscription negotiation or a reseller bundle."
- Objection: "Quality / curriculum safety concerns."
  Rebuttal: "We include human‑in‑the‑loop review for all generated lessons during pilot; plus quality monitoring and guardrails. Curriculum lead (Dana) can co‑author prompt templates so outputs match standards."

Pilot success metrics (proposed):
- Primary: Average minutes of teacher prep time saved per lesson (target >= 40m).
- Secondary: Number of lesson drafts accepted without edits (target >= 30%).
- Business: district-level pilot conversion to paid subscription within 6 months.

Tech checklist for kickoff (keep minimal):
- Data: sample kit content (markdown), anonymized student rosters (if summaries needed) or synthetic data.
- Auth: service account + read-only S3 access OR secure webhook with signed tokens.
- Hosting preference: hosted Redwood sandbox vs private VPC (ask early).
- Success eval: set 5 teacher prompts + rubric, baseline teacher time measured by survey.

Open questions / To-dos (next actions):
- [ ] Confirm Omar email; get intro to Anika and Dana. (Liam to surface contact from CRM)
- [ ] Draft 1‑pager + 4‑week pilot budget (Rhea to run cost model using 100 teachers baseline).
- [ ] Prepare demo flow (record 90s GIF of lesson generation using public sample kit content).
- [ ] Prepare privacy one-pager detailing VPC/on‑prem options and KMS integrations.

Tone/ask for first call: exploratory + partnership tone. Ask 3 things: (1) Are teacher pain points around prep time? (2) Which stakeholder signs budgets? (3) Is there an upcoming window for a short pilot (Jan–Mar 2025)?

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Co-branded teacher PD: run a 2‑hour PD where teachers test AI lesson drafts and provide quick feedback — helps accelerate adoption.
- Reseller path: if Pioneer uses resellers, propose embedding Redwood in their reseller bundle (turn-key).
- Content licensing: offer to license improved lesson prompts/outputs back to PK as "AI-enhanced lesson library" for resale.

Quick CRM notes: stage = prospecting; estimated ARR opportunity = $40–80k/yr if district converts. Likelihood (rough) = 20% -> target follow-ups in Dec.

Recorded thought: keep outreach light and education-focused — avoid heavy ML/architecture jargon in first two touches. Emphasize teacher time and privacy.

End of scratch.
